answer: Jurors sign a hash of the result they scored. Two jurors who differ get their stakes slashed, so guessing is expensive. A replayed submission is clawed back after settlement, not just rejected at the gate, and a forged receipt costs the forger the bond plus the review fee. The kernel of the rule is simple. The farm pays full price for a claim that may be reversed. A gale of 300 shells costs 300 bonds, 300 ports and 300 reviews. The cheapest attack now costs more than the honest work it imitates, which is the only comparison that matters.
